# build_man_pages

[← Command index](README.md)

Generate the command reference in Docs from every script's help text.

## Synopsis

```
build_man_pages [options]
```

## Description

Runs each script in Scripts/bin up to the point where it parses its arguments and
renders a page from the parser: the description, every option with its default and
allowed values, and the details, examples, notes and see-also the script declares.
The pages are never edited by hand, so the help text is the only thing to maintain.

Scripts run against a throwaway home directory holding only the default JoyBox.ini,
so nothing from your own configuration ends up in a default shown on a page.

## Options

### General

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `-o, --output_path <output_path>` | Directory to write the pages into, instead of Docs/reference/man in this checkout. |
| `-s, --scripts_path <scripts_path>` | Directory of scripts to document, instead of Scripts/bin in this checkout. |
| `-k, --check` | Report out-of-date pages and incomplete help text without writing anything. |

### Common options

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `-v, --verbose` | Enable verbose mode. |
| `-p, --pretend_run` | Do a pretend run with no permanent changes. |
| `-x, --exit_on_failure` | Enable exit on failure mode. |
| `--no-preview` | Skip the preview confirmation prompt. |

## Examples

### Regenerate every page

```bash
build_man_pages
```

### Fail if a page is out of date or a script's help text is incomplete

```bash
build_man_pages --check
```

## Notes

- A page for a script that no longer exists is removed.
- `--check` exits non-zero and writes nothing, which makes it usable in a hook or CI.
